claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game features a sequence of boss fights with limited exploration in between.

citations.review_text: It's just a boss rush. That's it. No map to run around and explore on. Nothing. Just go from boss A to boss B. Nothing in between.

Black Myth: Wukong, this is a game that looked very interesting to me for a few months, and I got to buy it recently. 
   Leaving aside the horrendous price for a story game, that's basically a boss beater (the exploration is quite awful, you go around from boss to boss), the game is very unoptimized for how it could be, very boring, the progression is straight forward and not very satisfying, and just generally not something I'd play if I have something else to run.
   Now for the Pros of the game:
- A fairly interesting combat system, 
- Good looking map
- Great graphics
- Fairly interesting story
- Occasional good and fun bossfights.
   For the cons of the game:
- The price,
- The pretty boring linear progression
- Some bosses are actually quite boring and annoying to fight
- Some locations are very annoying to go trough for absolutely no reason.
- The combat is pretty much the same everytime, which could be a pro if you don't like changing often, but for me it did get quite boring.
- How hard it is to run the game (The game relies on upscaling features.)

Overall, I'd give it a about a 5/10. It is not something I would definitely recommend, but I can't say it's completely bad either. I had very high hopes for this game, so perhaps being let down made me a little upset. Objectively speaking, If you catch the game on a good discount, you should try it, else I would refrain. I haven't finished the game, but I just can't continue playing it, atleast at this time.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that specific bosses require utilizing designated items or spirits, such as the Wind Tamer or Weaver's Needle, to bypass difficult mechanics or disadvantageous states.

citations.review_text:
If you like Easter Egg hunts, this game is for you. Just so you know, I'll let it all flat for you. You cannot, CAN ... NOT ... beat bosses without doing arbitrary wild goose chase easter egg hunts without getting the following items. Many have tried, all have failed. So let me point out the gimmicks of this game.

Chapter 2 (Yellow Wind Sage): Wind Tamer — Stops the arena-shrinking tornado storm.

Chapter 3 (Yellowbrow): Fire Mantle (or Weaver's Needle) — Helps negate his annoying golden invulnerability state and lightning AOE.

Chapter 4 (Hundred-Eyed Daoist Master): Weaver's Needle — The worst offender. Halfway through, he creates a golden domain that caps your maximum stamina at ~20% and disables your spells. Without the Needle (hidden behind a secret boss area in a mountain), you're basically forced to fight him with no stamina and no magic.

Chapter 5 (Red Boy / Yaksha King): Plantation Fan — Quenches his massive, arena-wide fire fields.

And this game is 6 chapters long, so for the majority of the game, you're running around doing crap that doesn't matter. Don't let all of these positive reviews fool you, they're all from China. The reviews may be in English, but these are chinese players. Sorry, but the clunky combat, lack of a ranged option when there are ranged enemies everywhere, and just poor level design killed it for me.

It all falls to the same premise. A lot of Western reviewers who rated it super high early on were rating the spectacle and scale—gorgeous graphics, 80+ boss designs, cinematic transformations—without having to sit down and suffer through late-game progression locks or clunky mechanics. When a game gets THIS much momentum, early discourse gets dominated by people telling you "You're playing it wrong" or "It's just hard like Dark Souls" whenever someone brings up legit criticisms like input buffering or invisible walls. And if this all sounds biased, I'll wrap it up for you in a neat little package. 

Looks like Next-Gen, Plays like 20…

(60 Hours on PS5)
I like the kit you can have in this game. but damn this can be frusturating to fight some bosses without knowing about the specific item or spirit that can help you against them. don't be shy or lazy to look for answers on youtube, it can save you tons of time. I do wish for a little more rewarding leveling up system, because there's kind of a power spike limit after the first 150-ish sparks.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game features invisible walls that block exploration throughout the environments.

citations.review_text:
Probably the best souls like out there that almost isnt a soulslike. The combat and bosses almost make it fall under the action game category, but has enough souls mechanics to still pass the vibe check.

Pros
An insane amount of bosses, some reskins/reused ones but the vast majority feel unique.

Combat is fast and fluid, and in your first playthrough enough differences in skill trees to feel the difference.

Visually gorgeous with an awesome story, especially if you have ready Journey to the West (not required)

Enough secret bosses and things to discover to satiate completionists without being obnoxious.

Way more forgiving than a traditional fromsoft game. Generous farming areas and less brutal punishment for death. But complex and difficult enough to still grab the hardcore souls fans. 

This would be a fantastic first step for anyone unsure about the genre as it has enough to do that you can really overcome anything it throws at you.

Cons

Exploration in the beautiful zones is sometimes suddenly blocked by invisible walls  :(

The final zone is large and open without really having a purpose behind it, visually gorgeous, but mechanically obnoxious.

Chapter 3 is like 50% of the game for some reason, weird pacing on that end of things.

All in all a 10/10 game for me and GotY for its year imo.

Black Myth Wukong is genuinenly kind of a mid game, but I still had an okay time with it.

The visuals are nice (when there are no UE5 stutters) and combat is decent with with a ton of enemies and bosses to fight. There is some variety in terms of spells and upgrade options, but the differences between the three combat stances didn't feel meaningful to me. 

Level design is not great, with invisible walls all over the place and no clear indication or consistent logic of which part of the visible level  is traversable and which part is not. Level design completely falls apart in the final chapter, which basically feels rushed / unfinished. The final boss was also  ridiculously overtuned.  

Don't come to this game for the story. I'm not familiar with the source material, but the writing felt like gibberish  90% of the time and character actions were nonsensical. At the end of the game I simply stopped trying and ended up just zoning out during narrative cutscenes. 

Overall I'd rate Wukong around a 7/10. If you're looking for a Soulslike game that's not from FromSoft there are better options to be found. If you keep your expectations in check, you will most likely still have a good time.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that completing quests and finding secret areas can easily be missed or locked out by progressing out of order.

citations.review_text:
I enjoyed this game, I'd probably give it an 8/10. Took me about 43 hours with good exploration, 56/81 achievements. I'll probably do new game+ but only once. Maybe revisit in a few years but probably not. Paid $45 but this is worth at full price. Doesn't seem to go on sale below that though. All I know about journey to the west is from Dragon Ball and Saiyuki, so I can't say I really followed the story that much. It was fun but seems like the gameplay is more the focus and the chapter endings didn't necessary seem overly related each time.

This game is kind of annoying in that you can be locked out of quests if you do things out of order. For example, I cleared a secret area boss but by doing so it locked me out of the area quest. This happened a few times, and I can only assume it's intended since it's a year past launch and I've seen people complaining about it. I really would've loved a map to know where I was, once you get into chapter 3 and 4 things really opened up. I got pretty worried that I was narrowly missing things, and that seems to be the case. Everywhere looks pretty similar so it's difficult. Since I paid for the game I would want to experience all of it, but the developers don't seem to agree... I saw a Chinese commenter on a review argue something to the point that "the way you can miss things mirrors journey to the west in that you don't get to see everything" or something to that effect. I appreciate the vision of the developers but I still think it's annoying if that's the intention. Unfortunately, I have the ability to always choose the direction of story content rather than side content in my pathing so I always have to backtrack to fully explore everything even if I'm not trying to.

Early on I got the weird impression that fighting the standard enemies was kind of pointless compared to the boss fights. It just seems like you can't really ever combo them meaningfully compared to the bosses and at the end of the day you could kill them easil…

finally beat the game and gotta say, it was really good, it feels like what lies of P was for souls, but instead this is an alternative to the new god of war games. every aspect of sound, music, world building and story where great. the bosses where mostly challanging. the performance of the game is great and i never had many stutters or frame drops. my only pet peeve for this game is some choices the devs made those being missable bosses for progressing the game, a set of armour that can not be fully crafted until new game+ and finally there is a hidden stance that can only be used at certain parts of the game which felt quite odd. other than those minor critics Its a solid 9/10 game.

To anyone who feels soulslike's are not your cup of tea, haven't tried any and do not intend to - this game could be the perfect gateway to the genre; without the jank and a lenient, more conservative learning curve. I went into this expecting a brutal challenge and came out pleasantly surprised at how balanced and enjoyable ALL of the boss fights were. There was no fight that took me more than an hour to beat and when I did, the satisfaction was immense. 

Game is absolutely gorgeous, the various tools at your disposal make the Sun Wukong power fantasy extremely satisfying and the visuals, boss designs are on point. My only issues with the game were its exploration, which often was unintuitive and made things VERY easy to miss. Also to anyone unfamiliar with the whole Journey to the West storyline, some lore aspects will require further reading and looking up. Overall, 10/10 and should have won GOTY no questions asked.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the game lacks difficulty settings to adjust the challenge.

citations.review_text:
[h1]A series of fundamental flaws hinder this unique game from ascending to Buddhahood.[/h1]

I flip-flopped a lot between the thumbs up and thumbs down. Overall, I think the positive aspects of this game (creativity, graphics, fun battles, etc.) may marginally outweigh the negatives...on a good day. I do not regret pouring 65 hours into Black Myth: Wukong, because it helped me prove to myself I could beat a tough game. Ironically, that experience also illustrates the game's biggest flaw: it asks for a lot while much of its narrative and thematic depth remains inaccessible without significant outside investment.

First off, the story is extremely vague and artsy. This likely works fine if the player either does not care about the plot or has a cultural familiarity with Chinese mythology. However, for people who assign high value to understanding story progression, heroic arcs, and motivations - you are in for a bad time. Unlike games that reward curiosity with lore (i.e. Elden Ring), Black Myth often replaces explanation with poetic ambiguity. This is especially true in the first few chapters where it is extremely important to ground the player: item and portrait descriptions are cryptic haikus that deepen confusion.

In addition to this, there is a VERY steep learning curve with no difficulty settings. I can even let this slide if there was a way to over-level to compensate or if each fight led to meaningful character development. But it seems like the fights were hard for the sake of being hard with no way to meaningfully "level up." The endless, exhausting boss gauntlet only helps you learn a skillset that is useless outside the immediate moment. Wukong plays at being "soulslike" while lacking the apparent depth or combat versatility that this genre of games promise. The fact that it is so poorly optimized for PC does not help either.

To understand the requisite background for this game, I watched a dozen YouTube videos and five full-length Chinese movies. It he…

Story scenes is pretty cinematic, well thought of character designs and good graphics optimisation. The only thing I dread is the difficulty settings, I wished there was like a difficulty selector for someone who is new to souls-like gameplay combat.

I loved many aspects of the game, it truly feels like a journey and it's spectacular all the way through. That being said, it also has some pacing issues and the difficulty spikes between certain bosses is crazy. I've finally rolled credits but I'm not looking forward to coming back, I hope the next one includes some kind of difficulty option or handles progression in a more linear and forgiving way.

WHAT. A. GAME.

Incredible from start to finish. Yes, there are still some performance issues and occasional FPS drops, but honestly, they feel insignificant compared to everything this game does right.

I loved diving deeper into Journey to the West and the way the story is told feels very FromSoftwarelike. You really need to pay attention, especially to the bosses’ stories. They’re not just fights; they’re a huge part of the experience.

This isn’t a game you should rush. Take your time, enjoy it day by day, and let the journey unfold naturally.

For me, this game came at the perfect time. I was feeling burnt out on gaming, and it completely pulled me back in. As you progress, everything intensifies—the bosses get tougher, the environments more complex, and the music and design just keep getting better.

If you have the time, you absolutely should play this game. Experience your own Journey to the West.

My Game of the Year for 2024.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the game is very demanding on hardware, requiring high-end specs or features like Frame Generation for stable frame rates.

citations.review_text:
Played this a while back when it released and completely forgot to leave a review, so here it goes.

After 100+ hours and 100% completion, I can confidently say Black Myth: Wukong exceeded every expectation I had.

The combat is incredibly satisfying, rewarding skill without ever feeling unfair... well, aside from the few times I almost punched a hole through my monitor. Even then, I always wanted to jump right back in. Every boss feels unique, and overcoming the toughest fights was one of the most rewarding experiences I've had in a long time.

The visuals are absolutely stunning, the soundtrack fits every moment perfectly, and the world is full of beautiful locations inspired by Chinese mythology. I can't really speak on the mythology itself since I don't know much about it, but the setting was gorgeous from start to finish.

I rarely spend this much time on a single game, but Wukong kept me coming back until there was nothing left to do. Every achievement felt earned, and finally seeing that 100% completion was incredibly satisfying. I'm also a huge soulslike fiend, so the struggle just made it even more fun.

If you're looking for an action RPG with challenging bosses, gorgeous environments, and some of the most satisfying combat around, this is an easy recommendation.

One thing to keep in mind, though: this game is very demanding. Make sure your PC meets (or preferably exceeds) the recommended specs if you want the best experience.

As a longtime Souls veteran, Black Myth: Wukong is easily one of the most impressive additions to this style of game.

The combat is absolutely top tier. Movement feels fluid, dodging is responsive, attacks have real weight behind them, and the combos are incredibly satisfying to pull off. I also love how freely the game lets you experiment. You can refund and redistribute your skill points at any shrine, swap spirits, change armor sets, and completely adjust your build whenever you need to adapt to a new boss or situation.

The boss design is one of the game’s biggest strengths. Visually, they are some of the most intricate and creative bosses I have ever seen, and many of them are just as mechanically fun to fight. The Chinese mythology, culture, music, and art direction also gave the game a style that really stood out to me. I played the entire game in Chinese with subtitles, and it made the experience even better.

It is also one of the most beautiful games I have ever played, although that comes with a serious performance cost. This game will push even high-end hardware extremely hard. With everything cranked up, ray tracing practically requires Frame Generation for a stable frame rate. Without ray tracing, I generally managed around 70 to 100 FPS, with occasional highs around 110.

Even with the demanding performance, this is still an easy 10/10 for me. I finished the entire game, immediately started New Game Plus, and I am already back in Chapter 3. I am still excited to unlock more gear, experiment with new builds, and take on the boss rushes, challenge modes, and gauntlets.

Highly recommended.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game suffers from technical issues, including crashes during cutscenes or related to DirectX 12 and Unreal Engine 5 stutter.

citations.review_text: Game has been beautiful and truly a breathtaking experience to play... that is until i got to chapter 3... Im at the final boss of chapter 3, FINALLY beat the boss after many, many attempts and the game crashed during the following cutscene and didnt create a checkpoint right after the boss was defeated, so of course, now i have to do the fight entirely over, despite now having the steam trophy for the boss. So now im mad enough to leave a review and im not too happy about it. This isnt the only time the game has crashed and im running a high end pc with updated drivers. This shouldn't be happening.

Amazing action game. Difficult, exacting yet highly rewarding. A few technical issues (crashes related to DX12 and UE5 stutter struggle) prevent this from being legendary. Overall a decent PC port, however, and well worth your time.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe encountering invisible walls that make exploration and navigation confusing and restrictive.

citations.review_text:
Look, I’ve put over 300 hours into this game and unlocked every single achievement, so nobody can say I didn't give it a fair chance. But even after all that dedication, I still absolutely cannot recommend it.
Let’s be real for a moment: Black Myth: Wukong is wildly overrated, largely driven by biased, hyper-inflated scoring from Chinese players turning it into a national pride project rather than judging it objectively as a piece of software. It simply does not live up to the insane hype, and compared to Hidetaka Miyazaki’s absolute masterpieces like Sekiro: Shadows Die Twice and Elden Ring, it falls incredibly short. To do my part in balancing out that artificially inflated score, I’m giving this a firm thumbs down.
At its core, Black Myth: Wukong is a beautifully packaged but fundamentally mediocre experience. Visually, it’s stunning, but that gorgeous wrapper hides some of the worst level design I've dealt with in years. You can never actually tell where you’re allowed to walk and where you’re going to smack directly into a frustrating invisible wall. The routes are incredibly confusing, giving you the illusion of a grand open space when you’re actually trapped in a tight maze of invisible boundaries. It makes exploration feel like a total chore; you spend so much time trying to find hidden corners and secret spots, only to end up disappointed and blocked by nothingness.
Even the regular enemy encounters are a total snooze fest. There’s zero highlight to fighting the standard mobs. They are sparsely scattered throughout the maps, and they’re either entirely too weak to care about or just annoyingly clunky and heavy. There’s no joy in navigating the world between major fights. The entire layout just feels like tedious, bloated filler designed to waste your time until you finally reach the next boss battle. If you’re expecting the meticulous world-building and flawless pacing of a FromSoftware title, you’ll be deeply disappointed. It’s pretty to look at, but hollo…

Great graphics. Good replayability because of build variety. Boss rush done right. It has it's issues like invisible walls and a bit of junk in the MCs moveset but holy smokes I can't stop playing it.

This is an unbelievably beautiful game, epic landscapes, tons of varied enemies with wonderfully animated move sets, and thoroughly interesting characters.  The references to Journey to the West abound and I was captivated by them.

This is married to some of the most miserable action gaming I've done in the last 20 years.  Your most used attacks feel weak.  You are often repeatedly hitting the enemy, and if they survive your initial onslaught, they continue their animations without noticing you are hitting them.  This is related to a system in the game, but it means you have to see the enemy's animations while your animations are playing in front of the enemy, making responding difficult.

The upgrade system is unreasonably vast and pointless since you can change it anytime you want. (Additionally, it's silly if thought of in context...could my character really forget how to use a stance but suddenly have super poison resist, and then reverse that a second later?)

Normal enemies you could probably beat with your eyes closed.  I don't have to learn any of their attacks because I can usually burst them down.  So much for all those animations, I rarely see them.

In my experience, bosses appear to be balanced around two types: figure out the win-quick gimmick, or your abilities rarely work and you have to chip down health while the boss throws out an entire feast of attacks. Many bosses took me 3 or less tries, some 5 or less tries, and then a few where 30/40+.  The difficulty spikes are there.

Clearly a tremendous amount of work went into this, but it appears to me like they made a wondrous animated movie, and then realized they had to throw some gameplay in there before they shipped it.
